items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to a rebate of real property taxes on certain residential real property in a city having a population of one million or more
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4136                  Revised 01/19/18

SPONSOR: LANZA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to a rebate of
real property taxes on certain residential real property in a city
having a population of one million or more

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Authorizes New York City to provide a rebate of a portion of the real
property taxes on owner occupied residential real property.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 - Amends heading of section 467-e of the real property tax
law, as added by section 1 of part V of chapter 60 of the laws of 2004.

Section 2 - Amends Subdivision 1 of section 467-e of the real property
tax law, as amended by chapter 483 of the laws of 2007.

Section 3 - Amends subparagraph 1 of paragraph a of subdivision 467-e of
the real property tax law, as added by section 1 of part V of chapter 60
of the laws of 2004.

Section 4 - Amends paragraph c of subdivision 3 of section 467-e of the
real property tax law, as added by section 1 part V of chapter 60 of the
laws of 2004.

Section 5 - Amends paragraph a of subdivision 4 of section 467-e of the
real property tax law, as amended by 483 of the laws of 2007.

Section 6 - Is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The city has enjoyed four consecutive fiscal years of budget surpluses,
including a projected $2.5 billion this current year and $3 billion the
previous fiscal year. The city should also share some of this prosperity
with the hard-working families who have helped to make it possible. A
tax rebate will provide much-needed relief to those homeowners struggl-
ing to pay bills, including seniors on fixed incomes, and could also
provide a boost to the local economy. And because we know economic
conditions often change, we feel it is imperative to provide this one-
time relief while we have the funds to do so.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017: S.4136 - Passed Senate
2016: S.7048 - 3rd Reading Calendar / A.9677 - Referred to Real Property
Tax.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Savings to property taxpayers.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Authorizes cities having a population of one million or more to provide a rebate during a specified city fiscal year of a portion of the real property taxes on owner occupied 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 family residential real property, or residential real property held in the condominium or cooperative form of ownership.
